scope: Standalone generated public Boolean quadratic systems at <=24 variables. No curve inputs, imported targets, scalar recovery, production integration or rho workflow.
contract: Projection retains the first 16 equation coordinates exactly. Every projected zero is checked against the complete original system; false hits continue in the same assignment order. All hits/checks/rejections are counted. Caps produce UNKNOWN, never false UNSAT. Scalar-source and native 16/64-point representations share the same identities and compiled four-bit Gray schedule.
selection: Five fixed treatments: scalar-source and native 16/64-point blocks, plus native dispatch with 16-point blocks through n20 and 64-point blocks above. Scalar source may be auto-vectorized; no instruction-count claim. No coefficient-dependent output crosses systems.
accounting: Every arm charges a fresh complete cold solve including encoding, narrowing, schedule construction, scan, original-system hit checks and temporary-workspace release, plus external validation. Returned diagnostic destruction, serialization, repeat-signature checks and common fixture/reference preparation are outside arm clocks and inside worker receipts. No timing subtraction.
ordering: Four fixed Fisher-Yates permutations per fixture, each followed by its exact reverse.
boundary: The reference is the pointwise fastest of the 52 complete solvers retained before this experiment. New scalar/native variants are separate implementations of the same new representation, not independent older references. Native-vs-scalar attribution is reported separately. No calibrated operation conversion or cryptanalytic floor is measured.
decision: Discovery only, no promotion. The final complete-solve criterion remains a paired 95 percent median-ratio lower bound >2.0 against the fastest retained reference in all 18 n16/n20/n24 x family x regression/holdout groups, with all cells complete and verified. Incremental >1.0 is separate. Any positive result requires unchanged-source confirmation on unused holdouts; no tuning after holdout timing.
encoding: One-pass domain validation and direct encoding of the first sixteen equation coordinates; omitted equations are still validated and used for every original-system check. No unsupported input silently falls back.
